name: Pixel Symmetry
mechanism:
This method analyzes pixel-level symmetry for image forensic analysis:

1. **Symmetry Detection**: Multiple types of pixel-level symmetry are detected — bilateral (mirror) symmetry, rotational symmetry, and translational symmetry (repetition). Symmetry is measured using normalized cross-correlation between the image region and its transformed version.

2. **Natural vs. Artificial Symmetry**: Natural images contain approximate symmetry (faces, architecture, natural objects) but never perfect pixel-level symmetry due to noise, lighting variation, and 3D perspective. The method measures symmetry precision — AI-generated images may show unnaturally precise symmetry (too perfect for a camera capture) per the analysis of Corvi et al. (2023).

3. **Local Symmetry Maps**: A per-pixel or per-region symmetry score map is computed showing the degree and type of local symmetry. The spatial distribution of symmetry reveals structural properties. AI generators may produce symmetry artifacts — unexpected symmetry patterns from the generator's architecture (e.g., U-Net skip connections creating symmetric features).

4. **Symmetry Breaking Analysis**: In natural images, physical factors break perfect symmetry — shadows, specularity, perspective foreshortening. The method checks whether expected symmetry-breaking factors are present. AI-generated images might maintain symmetry where physical factors should break it.

5. **Symmetry Feature Scoring**: Symmetry features (precision, spatial distribution, type frequency, symmetry-breaking correspondence) are combined into a forensic score. The score measures how well the image's symmetry properties match expectations for natural photography versus AI generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through pixel symmetry analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used

references.title: Corvi et al. (2023). On the Detection of Synthetic Images Generated by Diffusion Models. ICASSP.
Wang, S.Y. et al. (2020). CNN-generated images are surprisingly easy to spot. CVPR.
